questions.q: Which constitutional article provides for the appointment of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers by the President of India?
questions.a: Article 75 of the Constitution of India governs the appointment of the Prime Minister and Ministers. A wrong answer shows confusion with other structural articles, such as Article 79 which defines Parliament or Article 52 which establishes the office of the President.

questions.q: Why is the Prime Minister referred to as the "Head of Government" while the President is called the "Head of State"? Explain the difference in their political roles.
questions.a: The President is the ceremonial head of state who acts on the advice of the executive, whereas the Prime Minister is the active head of government who directs national policies, day-to-day administration, and legislative agendas. A wrong answer reveals the common misunderstanding that the President runs the government ministries and makes executive policy decisions.

questions.q: If a political party wins 275 elected seats in the 543-member Lok Sabha, what immediate constitutional step does the President take regarding the formation of the government?
questions.a: The President invites the leader of the party with the majority (275 seats) to form the government and appoints that leader as Prime Minister, then appoints other ministers on the Prime Minister's advice. A wrong answer indicates a misconception that the President independently selects any Member of Parliament to become Prime Minister regardless of party majority.

questions.q: How does the principle of "collective responsibility" operate within the Union Cabinet led by the Prime Minister?
questions.a: Collective responsibility means all ministers share joint accountability to the Lok Sabha for government policies and decisions; if a no-confidence vote passes, the entire Cabinet must resign. A wrong answer shows a failure to grasp that Cabinet decisions bind all ministers, even those who may have expressed private disagreements during internal meetings.

questions.q: Evaluate a scenario where the Prime Minister advises the President to dismiss a cabinet minister who publicly criticizes a government policy. Is this action constitutionally valid under the parliamentary system?
questions.a: Yes, this action is valid because ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President on the advice of the Prime Minister, and cabinet solidarity is vital for executive stability. A wrong answer indicates a belief that individual ministers possess independent tenure protected from the Prime Minister's leadership authority.

questions.q: Design a short advisory note explaining to a newly elected Member of Parliament how the Prime Minister coordinates policies across different ministries like Finance, Defense, and External Affairs.
questions.a: The advisory note should highlight that the Prime Minister allocates portfolios, resolves inter-ministerial disputes, sets the legislative agenda, and provides unified leadership across all departments. A poor answer focuses solely on ceremonial duties or treats each ministry as completely isolated from executive coordination.
